Found live 2026-07-29 while validating MPI-394 on a fresh CPU Pod: the user pressed Install on SDXL NSFW and the tile sat on 'Queued...' with nothing else installing. Proven from the live app: /comfy/downloads/status held NO sdxl-nsfw job at all (only engine:assets and klein-4b, both complete) and /comfy/downloads/active returned {models:[],engine:false} - so the POST never fired. Installs are serialised through a client-side promise chain gated on _inFlight (downloadService.js:76, MPI-184); 'queued' is only set when _inFlight > 0, so something held the chain. The only other start() in the session was engine:assets (drift heal logged nothing, no generation ran, App Library never opened) - so its chain link had not settled DESPITE download:complete having fired, which the completion toast proves. That is only possible if the listener was armed after the event. Root: run() armed _awaitDownloadDone INSIDE the post-POST .then(), but routes/downloadManager.js calls _startPendingDeps() BEFORE res.json() (register-before-respond, G8) and a fully-satisfied install goes terminal right there - 0 queued deps, nothing to download. The terminal broadcast therefore beats a listener armed after await res.json(). _awaitDownloadDone then burns its full 30-MINUTE ceiling with _inFlight pinned at 1, and every install clicked in that window sits at 'queued' forever - with no revert timer, because downloadService.js:90 arms one only for 'pending'. SHIPS TO USERS: _installRemoteEngineAssets re-runs on the first connect of EVERY session and is a pure no-op once the volume already holds the weights, so the common case (any session after the first) is the one that wedges, and the victim is the first model install after connecting to a Pod. NOT caused by the earlier volume-full session; a fresh volume would HIDE it, because a real 1.76GB download always lands after the listener is armed. Second, cosmetic half of the same trigger: notificationService announced 'engine:assets installed.' - a raw internal job id - as a toast and, unfocused, an OS notification, on every connect, even though shell.js states the heal must run silently.
